item.title: What the mobility deal between the EU and India will mean for skilled workers
item.description: As part of the landmark trade agreement announced on January 27th, the EU and India adopted a ‘mobility framework’ that aims to make it easier for Indian students, researchers and young professionals to move to the EU.

item.title: Inside Sweden: Is the sudden media coverage of deportations having an effect?
item.description: The Local’s Acting Editor Becky Waterton reflects on the opposition’s attempted campaign to end teen deportations before running through the other stories The Local has covered this week.

item.title: UK confirms ETA price hike for European travellers as rules set to toughen
item.description: The UK government is set to further increase the cost of the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) for travellers from Europe, coinciding with the implementation of tougher entry rules.

item.title: Climate activist group files second lawsuit against Sweden
item.description: A group of climate activists said Friday they were filing another lawsuit against the Swedish state for alleged climate inaction, after the Supreme Court threw out their case last year.

item.title: What do Europeans really think about immigration?
item.description: Growing political polarisation means that debate about immigration is boiled down to 'pro' or 'anti'-immigration positions, but new surveys reveal that European public opinion is a little more nuanced than that.

item.title: Lawyer says Sweden's plan to revoke residencies 'illegal on multiple counts'
item.description: There are so many reasons why Sweden's proposed law to revoke existing permanent residencies would be illegal that it's hard to believe those pushing it seriously intend it to happen, immigration lawyer Tomas Fridh tells The Local.

item.title: All the odd things you can borrow from a Swedish library
item.description: When you hear the word ‘library’, you probably think of borrowing books and maybe the odd film. But what about a ukulele, a sewing machine, or even tickets to the opera?

item.title: How can you watch the 2026 Winter Olympics on Swedish TV
item.description: The Winter Olympics, which this year takes place in Milan and Cortina, is arguably a bigger deal for Swedes than the summer variety. Where can you follow the action on Swedish TV?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Government delays language tests for citizenship by a year, leader of Swedish Armed Forces calls for European nuclear deterrent, and other news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: TELL US: What is the best district for foreigners in Stockholm?
item.description: From upmarket Östermalm and Nacka to more socially mixed areas like Bredäng or Kista, Stockholm has a huge number of different districts to choose from. We want to hear from readers about which is best for foreigners.
